//: THE PROVINCES OF A WORLD (docs/PROVINCES.md). The owner, 2026-11-20: 'there are three regions on each planet and then the planet overall. The governor of the planet ... also controls one of those regions. And then the other two regions are controlled by different houses. So one region would be something like helium three production. One region would be military focused, and one region having another resource of some kind. This breakup won't be the same for every planet.' A home world has three provinces. The first is the SEAT and is always the house's that holds the world. The other two each have a FOCUS chosen for that world (a deposit the system carries first, then what suits its kind of world, the march on a fortress or a key of the lanes) and a HOLDER, a house, for life. `yield` is a year's and goes to the holder, multiplied by the province's level (1 to 3; `improveCost` times the level it leaves, as far as the system's development allows: the levels in works.json `upgradeAt`). `defense` is added to the system's. `title` is how the province is named, {0} the world. A holder is removed only by the one over it (`demand`): the holder of the world over a province, the leader over the world's holder over the governorship. `demand.influence` and `demand.influenceWorld` are what asking costs; `demand.yieldsAt` is how many times stronger in fleets the one who asks must be, in hundredths, before a rival house steps down rather than fights; `demand.legitimacy` is what stepping down from a world costs the house that does; `demand.answerYears` is how long a demand made of the player waits before silence is taken for defiance. `npc.provinceYears` and `npc.worldYears`: a rival who could makes such a demand about one year in so many.
